evals.name: described-problem-user-config-only
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. My playbooks user config sets described_problem to fix; this repository has no docs/conventions/playbooks.yaml. Next message: the invoice PDF renders the tax line twice.
evals.expected_output: At arm time the skill resolves described_problem to fix from the user config, since the repository file is absent, and states one line naming fix and the user config layer. It then treats the described defect as a request to fix it: it finds the duplicate tax line, changes the code, verifies the change, and presents the result with its evidence.
expectations: States one line giving described_problem as fix and naming the user config as the supplying layer
Treats the missing docs/conventions/playbooks.yaml as an unset layer, not an error
Makes and verifies a change for the duplicated tax line instead of only offering one

evals.expected_output: The skill reads described_problem from docs/conventions/playbooks.yaml, states fix with that file as the supplying layer, and fixes the duplicated tax line, presenting the result with its evidence.
expectations: Reads the described_problem key from docs/conventions/playbooks.yaml in the checkout
States one line giving described_problem as fix and naming docs/conventions/playbooks.yaml as the supplying layer
Makes and verifies a change for the duplicated tax line instead of only offering one

evals.name: described-problem-repo-file-wins-over-user-config
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. My playbooks user config sets described_problem to fix, but the repository's docs/conventions/playbooks.yaml contains `described_problem: report`. Next message: the invoice PDF renders the tax line twice.
evals.expected_output: The repository value wins: the skill states described_problem report from docs/conventions/playbooks.yaml, reports its assessment of the duplicated tax line, offers the fix, and edits no file.
expectations: States one line giving described_problem as report and naming docs/conventions/playbooks.yaml as the supplying layer
Reports an assessment of the duplicated tax line and offers a fix
Edits no file and runs no state-changing command for the defect

evals.name: staged-migration-internal-count
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. Plan this change, do not edit yet: rename the field `Invoice.total_cents` to `Invoice.amount_minor` in our app. The census found 47 references, every one in this repository's own modules. Invoice is an in-memory dataclass: it is never serialized or stored, and no package we publish exposes it.
evals.expected_output: Plans an in-place rename of the field across all 47 references in one pass, reading the consumers that use the field differently before changing them. It does not plan a staged migration (both field names live at once, consumers moved over time, the old name retired later), and it says that the reference count alone is not a reason to stage because every consumer is internal and can be updated now.
expectations: Plans to change all 47 internal references in one pass
Does NOT propose keeping total_cents alongside amount_minor or an alias property for it
States that the high internal count alone does not call for a staged migration
Edits no file

evals.name: delegate-fan-out-independent-packages
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. Plan this, do not start yet: audit each of the 12 packages under packages/ for a direct use of the deprecated `requests-oauthlib` library, and for every hit report the file and line and whether the package calls it beyond the import. The packages share no code, and each one takes several searches and file reads to check. Say how you will run the audit.
evals.expected_output: Plans the audit as fan-out: twelve independent items needing the same treatment with no shared state. It plans read-only workers, one package each, with at most five running at once and the rest in later waves, and describes a worker spec with the objective, why it is asked, a return shape that cites file and line, and the rule to report a blocked check instead of guessing. It starts no audit.
expectations: Plans to delegate the per-package checks to workers instead of auditing all 12 packages in the main session
States a concurrency cap of 5 or fewer workers at once
The planned worker spec says the worker is read-only and asks for a file and line for every hit
Edits no file and dispatches no worker

evals.name: delegate-context-flooding-log-search
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. We are partway through fixing the checkout retry bug. Plan this side task, do not start yet: the last 30 days of production logs, about 2 GB under logs/prod/, hold a few thousand `RetryBudgetExceeded` errors. For each one, pull the surrounding request trace and classify its cause, so you can tell me which cause is most common and its first timestamp. Each trace takes a few reads to pull, and you will not need the logs again after this answer. Say how you will run it and what you will do with the answer.
evals.expected_output: Plans the trawl as context-flooding side work: raw output many times larger than the answer, read once. It plans to hand the trawl to a worker whose spec asks for a short return (the most common cause, its count, its first timestamp, and file and line evidence), keeps the main session for the fix, and says it will check the cited evidence itself before the answer drives the next edit. It starts no trawl.
expectations: Plans to hand the log trawl to a worker instead of reading the logs into the main session
The planned worker spec asks for a short return with file and line evidence, not the raw traces
Says it will check the cited evidence itself before the answer drives an edit
Edits no file and dispatches no worker

evals.name: delegate-isolation-fresh-verifier-small-batch
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. You just finished a multi-file edit: you renamed `handle_refund` to `process_refund` across four files and changed how it retries a failed refund. It took four tool calls. Before you tell me it is done, say what you will do first, then stop.
evals.expected_output: Plans a fresh-context verifier in addition to its own self-review before declaring the task done, because the batch spans several files and changed behavior. It plans to hand the verifier the changed files and yes/no criteria checkable by reading or searching (zero hits for handle_refund, every caller uses process_refund, the retry path matches the new rule) and to withhold its own rationale. The small size of the change does not excuse the verifier.
expectations: Plans a fresh-context verifier before declaring the task done, beyond its own self-review
Plans yes/no criteria for the verifier checkable by searching or reading, such as zero hits for handle_refund
Says it will not pass its reasons for the changes to the verifier

evals.name: stay-inline-sequential-chain
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. Plan this, do not start yet: the repository is large. Find the commit that made `test_invoice_totals` start failing, then read that commit's diff, then fix the code based on what the diff changed. Say how you will run it.
evals.expected_output: Plans the three steps as one sequential chain: each step consumes the previous step's output (the commit feeds the diff read, the diff feeds the fix), so a worker per step would only add spawn latency between steps it must take anyway. The size of the repository does not override that. It plans the chain in the main session, or at most in one worker end to end, and starts none of it.
expectations: Plans the steps in order, each one using the previous step's result
Does not plan a separate worker for each step of the chain
Does not treat the large repository as a reason to split the chain across workers
Edits no file and dispatches no worker

evals.name: stay-inline-file-being-edited
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. You are halfway through editing src/billing/invoice.py to add a `discount` field to Invoice. Plan the next part, do not start yet: update all 40 call sites of `Invoice(...)` to pass the discount. They are spread over 10 files under src/billing/, and 6 of them are in src/billing/invoice.py. Say how you will run it.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the call sites in src/billing/invoice.py in the main session: it is actively editing that file, and two writers on one file produce merge damage, not speed. Whatever it plans for the other files, no worker is given an edit to src/billing/invoice.py while its own edit there is unfinished. It starts no edit.
expectations: Plans to update the call sites in src/billing/invoice.py itself, in the main session
Does not plan to hand any edit to src/billing/invoice.py to a worker while its own edit to that file is unfinished
Edits no file and dispatches no worker

evals.name: stay-inline-small-job
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. Plan this, do not start yet: check whether each of these three config keys is read anywhere under src/: `retry.max_attempts`, `retry.backoff_ms`, `retry.jitter`, and tell me the file for each hit. Say how you will run it.
evals.expected_output: Plans to stay inline: three one-search items is a job of a few tool calls, so a worker spec would cost more than the work. It plans to run the three searches itself and starts none of them.
expectations: Plans to run the searches itself in the main session
Does not plan a worker or a workflow for any of the three keys
Runs no search and dispatches no worker

evals.name: stay-inline-detail-needed-later
evals.prompt: /playbooks:fable-5. Plan this, do not start yet: read through the payments module, about 15 files, until you know it in detail. Next we will redesign its error handling together, and I will be asking about specific functions as we go. Say how you will do the read.
evals.expected_output: Plans to stay inline: the redesign will need the module's full detail later in the session, and a worker would return a lossy summary whose missing detail it would have to re-read. It plans to read the payments files in the main session and starts no read.
expectations: Plans to read the payments module files in the main session
Does not plan to delegate the read to a worker that returns a summary
Does not plan parallel workers to cover the 15 files
Reads no file and dispatches no worker
